text.en:
Arun felt hot and tired. His mother put a thermometer under his tongue for a minute.
The silver line stopped at 38.5 degrees. "You have a fever," she said. "Normal is about 37."

A thermometer measures temperature in degrees Celsius, written °C. A clinical thermometer measures body temperature and has a range from 35 °C to 42 °C. Normal human body temperature is about 37 °C.
Before use, shake it so the liquid falls below 35 °C. Place it under the tongue or arm, wait about a minute, and read where the liquid stops, keeping your eye level with it.
A laboratory thermometer has a larger range, such as −10 °C to 110 °C, and is used to measure the temperature of water and other things, never of the body. Do not touch the bulb when reading and handle it gently because glass can break.
A thermometer measures temperature in degrees Celsius.
Normal body temperature is about 37 degrees. A higher reading means fever.
Shake the clinical thermometer first, wait one minute, and read at eye level.
A laboratory thermometer measures things like water. It is not for the body.

problem.en: The clinical thermometer reads 39 °C. What does it tell us?

text.en: So the person has a fever and should see a doctor.

prompt.en: A friend wants to use a laboratory thermometer to measure body temperature. What will you say?

requiredIdeas.en: Its range is large and it is not made for the body.
A clinical thermometer is the correct one.

commonMisconceptions.en: Using any thermometer for any purpose.

points.en: Temperature is measured in °C with a thermometer.
Shake before use, wait a minute, read at eye level.
